newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end higher, selected firms soar.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end higher, selected firms soar.

text.p: Spanish stocks ended higher on Friday, overturning early losses after the Bank of Spain left its key money rate unchanged, helped by rallies in selected firms, dealers said.
The general index rose 2.79 points, 0.71 percent, to 394.20 and the Ibex added 32.77 points, 0.73 percent, to 4,544.34.
Telecoms equipment firm Amper added 120 pesetas to 2,090 in busy trade fueled by talk of a cash return to shareholders and an imminent dividend payment.
But the company told Reuters it was not planning to give cash back to shareholders.
Tabacalera ended up 200 pesetas to 4,890 on renewed rumours that it would soon pass on July's surprise government tax hike to final cigarette prices in the shops.
Repsol added 60 pesetas to 4,495, a climb based on fundamentals after a sustained share price slump, dealers said.
Short-term, the outlook generally remains positive.

"The market's very firm, people are still backing the bourse and now the logical thing is to consolidate prices, but if foreign references are positive, money will continue to flow in for equities," said one dealer.
